title: Roll a fallen robot dog off its propping legs to take its battery out of the belly
instruction: The quadruped robot has fallen and its battery is flat. Take the battery out and put it on the charging pad.
context: A robot dog of the kind sent into collapsed or hazardous sites can carry its battery in the belly, and its crew rolls it over to change it. Powered off after a fall it does not lie on its side: it props itself on its loose legs, belly down and tilted, the bay facing down toward the ground, and pushed at the trunk it slides on its legs instead of turning. Unlike TK-JJD7XA (packs swapped in an open bay on top) the bay must first be brought up, and unlike TK-4J8HRQ (a humanoid rolled over a free arm) this body has to be rolled over the legs it props on, by the handles of its high side, before the battery can be drawn. Robots do this where people are kept out.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Pad: a plywood board 1 cm thick clamped to the table, x 3 to 48, y -30 to 30, top painted earth brown (friction about 0.6); its far strip, x 43 to 48, covered with flat artificial-grass mat. Charging pad: a dark grey plastic plate 14 x 14 x 0.6 cm (friction 0.6) on the pad, x 8 to 22, y -27 to -13. Robot: a passive 1:2 model of a mid-size robot dog, 1.90 kg, grey PLA shell (friction 0.6; rubber feet 0.9) on steel pin hinges with hard end stops, no motors or springs, every joint free to fall. Trunk 18.8 long x 4.7 wide x 5.7 tall (0.73 kg, with a round head 5 cm across on its front); four legs, each an abduction hinge at the trunk's corners (9.7 cm fore and aft of the centre, 2.3 cm out, a housing 4.6 cm across, 85 g), a thigh 10.65 long x 1.7 x 1.2 (144 g) on a hinge 4.8 cm further out and a calf rod 10.65 long x 1.25 across with a rubber foot ball 2.2 across (30 g). Ranges (degrees): abduction -60 to 60; thigh -90 to 200 (front), -30 to 260 (rear); knee -156 to -48 (never straight). A black PLA handle over each hip (friction 0.8): an 8 mm rung 4.5 cm long on two 5 mm brackets from the trunk's top edge, 1.2 cm above the trunk's top, 7.5 cm fore or aft of the centre and 5.7 cm out. Battery: a slate-blue PLA block 10.8 x 3.0 x 2.15 cm, 140 g (friction 0.4), in a bay 11 x 3.2 x 2.2 cm deep in the belly (flush with it), with an orange grip tab 3.6 x 0.4 x 1.0 cm standing out of its face (friction 0.8); a magnetic catch holds it seated up to a 3 N pull. Start: the robot lies along y, head toward +y, trunk centre at (33, 0, 8.0), fallen on its right side and settled as it does by itself: resting on its right hip housings and thighs (the right legs splayed out) and on its left calves, belly 140 degrees from straight up (the bay facing the arms and 50 degrees below level, its tab 3.9 cm above the pad), back tilted away from the arms; the battery seated.
scoring: 0 if at any time the lowest point of the robot's trunk (with its head and handles) is more than 6 cm above the ground (the pad's top): it was lifted; or if, the first time the battery leaves its catch (its centre more than 4 mm from its seat), no gripper point is within 2 cm of it: it fell or was knocked out. Otherwise the end state counts, and is 0 unless the robot's trunk and the battery are at rest (neither centre moved more than 2 mm over the last second) and released (no point of either gripper, and no point along either arm from its shoulder joint to its palm, within 5 cm of the robot or the battery), both for each of the last 20 control steps (1 s at 20 Hz), and unless the battery is out of its bay (its centre at least 3 cm from its seat). Then: 1.0 if the battery's whole outline, its grip tab included, lies over the charging pad and its lowest point is within 5 mm of the pad's top; 0.5 otherwise. A full score ends the trial once it has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Lay the robot on its right side along its marks and let it settle onto its legs (it props itself in under a second); seat the battery first.
fidelity: Rigid links, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control; hinges limp (light damping, no friction or spring), hard end stops. Sizes, masses and joint ranges are a 1:2 scale of a public mid-size quadruped model (lengths x 1/2, masses x 1/8); shapes are boxes, capsules, cylinders and spheres. The magnetic catch is a 3 N force toward the seat while the battery is within 3 mm of it. The turf strip is drawn on the rigid pad.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right arm went to the charging pad and the arms hovered near the robot without touching it; it stayed propped on its legs); demo: 1.0
